raw.source: US BIS - Department of Commerce Rescinds Biden-Era Firearms Rule, Restoring Common Sense to Export Controls on Civilian Firearms
raw.content_en: The US Department of Commerce (BIS) has rescinded the Biden-era firearms export rule, easing export controls on civilian firearms, ammunition, and related parts. For China-based exporters and traders, this signals a recalibration of US export licensing for firearms and components under ECCN/ITAR-adjacent categories. Exporters should re-verify classification of firearms, optics, and parts against the revised USML/CCL boundary, confirm whether items previously requiring licenses now qualify for license exceptions, and screen all parties against BIS Entity List and denied persons lists. Section 301 tariffs and HTS alignment remain applicable to China-origin goods, and dual-use optics or night-vision components may still face heightened scrutiny. Maintain end-use/end-user documentation and monitor Federal Register updates for effective dates and transition provisions.
raw.content_zh: 美国商务部（BIS）撤销了拜登时期的枪支出口规则，放宽对民用枪支、弹药及相关零部件的出口管制。对于中国出口商和贸易商而言，这意味着美国对枪支及零部件的出口许可要求出现调整。出口商应重新核对枪支、光学器件及零部件的分类，确认其在美国军品清单（USML）与商业管制清单（CCL）之间的归属变化，核实此前需许可的项目是否现可适用许可例外，并对所有交易方进行BIS实体清单和被拒绝人员名单筛查。中国原产货物仍适用301关税及HTS归类要求，两用光学或夜视部件可能仍面临更严格审查。应保留最终用途/最终用户证明文件，并关注联邦公报关于生效日期和过渡条款的更新。

checklist.desc: Re-verify USML/CCL classification of firearms, ammunition, optics, and parts against the rescinded rule; confirm ECCN or EAR99 status and any license exception eligibility.
Flag optics, night-vision, and precision components that may remain controlled dual-use items; obtain technical specifications and end-use statements.

checklist.task: BIS Entity List & denied party screening
checklist.desc: Screen all buyers, consignees, and intermediaries against BIS Entity List, Denied Persons List, and OFAC SDN; retain screening records.
Map 10-digit HTS lines for firearms and parts, confirm Section 301 additional duty exposure, and document country of origin and value build-up.
Prepare and retain end-user certificates and non-re-export statements consistent with revised EAR licensing posture.
Track Federal Register effective dates and transition provisions; update internal compliance manuals and training accordingly.
